13	// >= 64 M-rows per issue, but one ViT sample is kSeq=17 rows. So the scalar
14	// "one CTA owns a batch slice, one sample at a time" model CANNOT use tensor
15	// cores. The TC path batches across samples: M = (sample × position) TOKEN rows.
16	// Each CTA owns a contiguous tile of SG_TUNED_TILE_M token rows; the tile

22	//   1. FULL (bidirectional) attention — NO causal mask. Every key position kj
23	//      contributes for every query qi (the decoder masked kj>qi). The fwd/bwd

27	//      (K=49 padded to 64). The CLS token (a learned [d] vector) is prepended at
28	//      position 0; pos[17] is a learned table added to all 17 positions.
29	//   3. CLS pos-0 HEAD — the final-norm + head + CE run on position 0 of each
30	//      sample (the decoder used the LAST position, kSeq-1).
31	//   4. kSeq=17 → kTileM a MULTIPLE OF 17 (and of 64, the wgmma atom). The least
32	//      such is LCM(17,64)=1088 (= 17 stacked m64 atoms = 64 samples × 17 pos).

121	**Required smem operand layout (`:250-259`).** For an `MN×16` bf16 operand, element `(mn,k)` lives at bf16 index `idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — i.e. K=16 is two stacked 8-wide core matrices, each an `MN×8` row-major block of 128-bit rows. The staging loops everywhere (model headers, self-test, tile_pipeline) must write this exact layout.
122	
123	**Fragment decode (`WgmmaAccum<N>` + `wgmma_frag_decode`, `:314-364`).** The per-thread fp32 accumulator holds `N/2` registers (PTX §<ip>.3). The authoritative decode maps `(tid_in_wg, reg i)` → `(row, col)`: the M=64 rows are partitioned warp-major (`row = 16*warp + lane/4 + 8*row_half`), and the N columns are held as n8 column slabs (`col = (lane&3)*2 + col_par + 8*slab`) (`:357-362`). Keeping ONE decode shared by the epilogue store and the gate's reference comparison eliminates the chance of a mismatched private decode (`:310-312`).
124	
125	**Fence/commit/wait choreography (`:366-403`).** `wgmma_fence()` (§<ip>.2) makes prior non-wgmma writes to the accumulator/operand-smem visible before the first issue; `wgmma_commit_group()` (§<ip>.5) batches issued MMAs into a group; `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` (§<ip>.6) blocks until ≤N groups remain — the epilogue must `wait_group<0>` before reading the accumulators.

The first issue uses `ScaleD=0` (overwrite, so a fresh accumulator needs no zeroing), the rest `ScaleD=1` (accumulate); one `wgmma_fence()` before the group, one `commit_group()+wait_group<0>()` after. The descriptor generator is a callback `gen(k)`, which is what lets the *same* mainloop serve both the unpipelined gate (fixed pre-staged array) and the pipelined gate (ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical numerics (`:603-609`). The per-N issue overloads (`wgmma_issue_n8/16/32/64/96/128`, `:441-561`) each name exactly `N/2` `+f` accumulator registers; N=128 (default tile, 64 regs) is the in/out/ff GEMM shape.

129	### 5. The cp.async multi-stage ring (`tile_pipeline.cuh` + the PIPE/STAGES macros)
130	
131	`tile_pipeline.cuh` adds the producer/consumer ring choreography on top of the wgmma engine, reusing `Mbarrier`/`cp_async_cg_16`/`cp_async_wait_group` rather than redefining them (`tile_pipeline.cuh:9-17`). It uses **cp.async (`.cg.16`), not TMA** — TMA is explicitly phase-2 (`:199-200`). A `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (`:142-189`) manages a Depth-stage ring of `(A 64×16 + B N×16)` bf16 tiles plus `2*Depth` mbarriers — a `full[s]` (producer arrives via `arrive_expect_tx` when a stage's loads are issued; consumer waits before wgmma) and an `empty[s]` (consumer arrives when done; producer waits before overwriting, WAR-safe) per stage (`:117-135`). Each barrier expects a **full warpgroup (128) of arrivals** — a per-warp `elect_one` would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock the parity wait, a bug called out explicitly (`:170-179`). `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16` (`:271-364`) splits the 256-thread CTA into WG0 (producer: cp.async-stages each K-tile, `:296-312`) and WG1 (consumer: wgmma in ascending k, `:313-360`), with the `setmaxnreg` register rebalance (producer few regs, consumer many) via `SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40 / SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS=232` (`:92-97, 289-294`). Determinism: the consumer issues the SAME ss-wgmma sequence in the SAME ascending-k order, so the pipeline only changes *when* an operand becomes available, not the math (`:265-269`).
132	
133	**The decoder's PIPE/STAGES macros** (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh`) wrap this into a tunable 3-way selector:
134	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_STAGES` (the base K-loop double-buffer depth; default 2, `:90-92`).
135	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE` — master 3-way selector, **baked at 1** (`:185-187`): `0` = the shipped S=2 ring verbatim (byte-identical PTX); `1` = entry (a), the SAME all-threads-stage/WG0-compute ring **deepened** to `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` slots (more cp.async groups in flight); `2` = entry (b), the full producer/consumer mbarrier engine transcribed from `tile_pipeline.cuh` (`:227-252`). The comment records the tournament verdict: **entry-a deeper ring won (+1.49×); entry-b PIPE=2 LOST (857 vs 618 ms)** (`:186`).
136	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` (2..4), **baked at 4** with PIPE=1 (`:188-190`).
137	
138	`kDecFwdStages = kDecFwdPipe ? FWD_STAGES : kDecTcStages` (`:261`), and `kDecRingStagesMax = max(fwd-ring, dW-ring)` sizes the smem allocation (`:268-269`). The three ring bodies are in `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`: the producer/consumer mbarrier engine (`:860-987`), the original S=2 double-buffer ring (`:988-1016`), and the deeper RS=3..4 ring (`:1017-1062`). The deeper ring keeps `RS-1` cp.async groups in flight via `cp_async_wait_group<RS-2>` in the steady region (drains the oldest tile) and `<0>` in the tail (`:1032-1061`). At S=2 the deeper loop collapses to `wait_group<0>` exactly, which is why PIPE=0 is byte-clean (`:173-175`).
139	
140	**The dynamic-smem path (`SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM`).** The static `__shared__ DecTcSmem` is hard-capped at 48 KB on H100 (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:478-485`); the deeper fwd/dX ring's `sA`/`sB` grow ∝ ring depth (`:386-387`) and the legal-max tile reaches 49.64 KB at S=4 (`:460-463`). The preprocessor gate `SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM = PIPE && (STAGES>2)` (`:464-468`) routes those configs to **dynamic smem** instead: `DecTcSmem` is placed in an `extern __shared__ char[]` pool (`:688-689`), the func is opted into `>48 KB` via `cudaFuncSetAttribute(..., cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, sizeof(DecTcSmem))` (`:1533-1535`), and occupancy ≥1 is certified against the real size against the **228 KB/SM** budget (`:476-477`). This is an allocation change only — identical layout / access pattern / fp32 accumulation order / wgmma issue sequence → parity by construction (`:439-442`). The dW path always keeps the synchronous (lambda-source) staging — it is staging-bound, not drain-bound, so a ring would be the wrong lever (`:782-783`).
141	
142	**The producer/consumer PIPE=2 variant** adds `2*kDecRingStages` mbarrier words `pipe_bars[]` to `DecTcSmem`, but `#if`-gated on the macro so on the shipped PIPE=0|1 builds the member is *entirely absent* and `sizeof(DecTcSmem)`/PTX is byte-identical (`:390-408`). The `SG_DEC_PIPE_BARS_ARG` macro expands to `, sm.pipe_bars` only under PIPE=2 and to nothing otherwise (`:420-424`), so the shipped tile-call sites are textually unchanged. The engine body (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:860-987`) makes WG0 the consumer (wgmma into `acc[]`, owns the epilogue) and WG1 the pure producer, with `bar_full`/`bar_empty` mbarriers each expecting 128 arrivals; the consumer issues `issue_k(g_atoms,k,RS)` in ascending k → the wgmma issue sequence and fp32 accumulation are bit-identical to PIPE=0 (`:876-887`).
143	
144	### 6. Decoder specifics
145	
146	- **Causal attention** — `dectc_forward_tile` runs per-sample causal self-attention (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1433`); the head is masked `kj > qi`, in contrast to ViT's bidirectional attention. The final-norm + head + CE run on the **last** position (`kSeq-1`).
147	- **Embedding counting-sort owner-scan** — the embedding gradient is a scatter-add of `dh0` into a small set of vocab rows. The H2 design (`:2418-2446`) uses a deterministic integer counting sort: `dectc_embed_build_lists` (`:2469-2527`) builds CSR offsets `row_start[V+1]` + a permutation `perm[T]` (token positions bucketed by vocab row, ascending-t within each row) once on CTA 0 in the P1 window. The consume `dectc_embed_owner_scan` is a flat grid-stride over all `V·d` output elements where element `(r,j)` walks only row r's tokens in ascending-t order, reading `dh0[perm[i]·d+j]`. This collapses work to `O(d·T)` with coalesced reads and keeps all 132 CTAs busy. **Determinism**: per-row accumulation is the same fixed ascending-t order as the old scan → bit-identical fp32, no atomics (`:2435-2439`). The build's per-(worker,row) cursor uses an ascending-worker prefix within a row so lower-t chunks land first — globally ascending t per bucket (`:2501-2513`).
148	- **dW split-K (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK`)** — chunks the dW `K=T` contraction across CTAs so the ~62% idle SMs in P2 do real work (`:86-88`). `dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk<N>` (`:2295-2339`) computes a PARTIAL over K-chunk `kc` of `G` into a per-(tile,chunk) scratch slot with a **floor-balanced partition** `k0=floor(kc·KS/G), k1=floor((kc+1)·KS/G)` — near-equal, summing to KS exactly for any KS≥G (a ceil split would leave a trailing empty chunk whose unwritten slot sums garbage; the floor never empties one, `:2288-2294`), with an explicit empty-chunk guard zeroing the slot (`:2318-2322`). `dectc_dw_reduce_splitk` (`:2343-2366`) then sums the G chunk-partials in **ascending kc** → deterministic. The default is now **G=1** (`:101`): with DW_STAGE=1 the single-CTA dW is 2.05× faster than G=2-scalar, making split-K (a scalar-dW grid-fill mitigation) obsolete (`:98-100`).
149	- **The DW_STAGE staging method (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE`, default 1)** — the dW GEMM is **staging-bound, not drain-bound**: ~97% of each K-step was the scalar transposed-strided operand gather, only ~3% the wgmma (`:117-124`). So the lever is faster *staging*, not pipelining the MMA. `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1` does a cheap grid-cooperative pre-transpose (`dectc_dw_transpose_operands`, `:2088`) writing each weight's dY/X once per step into a **contiguous K-major** scratch (`dYt[Nout,K], Xt[Kin,K]`, K-contiguous + 16B-aligned), so the dW then builds `DecGmemTileSrcA/B` over it and reuses the existing cp.async ring's 16-byte coalesced copies instead of the 2-byte strided gather (`:132-143`). It changes transport only — fp64 parity + A/A/A by construction. `kDecDwTransposeActive = (DW_STAGE==1) && (DW_SPLITK==1)` (`:1994`); when active, an extra B1b barrier fences the transposed operands before any dW GEMM read (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:910-915`).
150	
151	### 7. ViT specifics
152	
153	ViT is a genuine rewrite (separate header `model_stage_vit_tc.cuh`) with four deltas vs the decoder twin (`:21-32`): (1) **full bidirectional attention** — no causal mask, every key contributes for every query (`:22-24, 764`); (2) patch-proj `Linear(49→128)` replaces token embedding, with a learned CLS token prepended at position 0 and a `pos[17]` table; (3) the CLS pos-0 head (final-norm + head + CE run on position 0, not the last); (4) `kSeq=17` forces `kTileM = LCM(17,64) = 1088` (17 stacked m64 atoms = 64 samples × 17 positions).
154	
155	**The B1 sub-tile lever (`SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S`, baked at 8).** Because the GEMM tile is locked at 1088 rows, at B=1024 there are only `n_tiles=16` P1 tiles, so **116 of 132 CTAs do zero P1 work and spin at B1** the whole fwd+bwd — tile-count-vs-SM quantization, the #1 ViT cost (51.2% of the step) (`:125-131`). This knob decouples the P1 *scheduling* granularity from the 1088 GEMM lock: P1 grid-strides over sub-tiles of **S whole samples** (`kSeq·S` rows) instead of whole 1088-row tiles, growing `n_tiles` ~`64/S`× so the idle CTAs pick up work and the B1 spin collapses (`:133-137`). S must stay a *whole-sample* count — never split a 17-row sample across CTAs, which would corrupt attention (`:137-141`). The sub-tile row count `kSeq·S` is generally not a multiple of 64, so the small GEMMs pad M up to `ceil(rows/64)·64` atoms with a runtime `m_real` row-guard making the pad rows inert and race-free (`:139-141, 373-391`). **Default 64** (== `kSamplesPerTile`) makes the build byte-identical (the `m_real` guard + runtime-m_atoms code is `#if`'d out at S==64, `:143-147`). The P1 loop using `kVitP1SubtileRows` is at `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:588-613`. **Parity**: dW/biases/cls/pos grads are byte-identical (P2 reads acts by global token row, contracts ascending-k independent of P1 tiling); the LN-affine γ/β grads + loss are valid fp32 reassociations absorbed by the 1e-4 reorder tol; A/A/A holds because S is a fixed deterministic partition (`:150-162`). The baked verdict: **S=8 is parity-clean (11/11 ViT cells × 3 seeds) and fastest — 4.02× vs S=64 OFF at d=2048/B=1024** (`:164-169`).
156	
157	ViT P2 is dW-output-stationary (`vittc_dw_run_tile` or split-K, `:642-648`) plus biases, the cls/pos owner-scan (`vittc_clspos_owner_scan`, `:656`), and the LN-vec reduce (`:657`).
158	
159	### 8. Mamba3 specifics
160	
161	Mamba3 (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh`) is the genuine Mamba-3 SISO architecture (arXiv 2603.15569, ICLR 2026) transcribed line-for-line from the fp64-verified oracle (`:8-15`). The mixer is a complex **exponential-trapezoidal selective scan** (Eq 25, the heart of the kernel):
162	
163	`v_t = Bbar_t ⊙ x_t; h_t = alpha_t·(R_t@h_{t-1}) + beta_t·(R_t@v_{t-1}) + gamma_t·v_t; y_t = Σ_{c,d} Cbar_t[c,d]·h_t` with `alpha=exp(dt·A), gamma=lam·dt, beta=(1-lam)·dt·alpha` per head and a 2×2 rotation `R(phi)` per complex coord (`:41-46`).

104	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
105	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,

280	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
281	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
282	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
283	cudaError_t mega_decoder_sg2_tc(
284	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
285	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
286	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,

303	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {

305	    // gru_state spans total*GH (GH=DecSG2Dims::gru_hidden); the layout is fixed by

307	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;

314	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;

324	
325	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
326	    FusedOptState st;
327	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
328	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
329	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
330	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
331	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
332	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
333	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
334	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
335	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
336	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
337	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
338	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
339	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
340	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
341	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
342	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
343	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
344	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;

346	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
347	    st.sg2_expert_W2 = expert_W2; st.sg2_expert_b2 = expert_b2;

# Phase-0b EXHAUSTIVE digest — Session archive + the UPGRADED L3-TC kernels + prebuilt binaries

**Area:** `claude_session_archive/` (195 jsonl), the `_dectc_codegen/` PTX-edit variant tree, the
baked perf levers in `csrc/fused/sm_90/`, the prebuilt `_ops.so`, and `CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md` /
`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md` / `SESSION_STATE.md` (the docs the prior grep-skim pass under-read).

**Method:** read the kernel-source lever blocks line-by-line; statically decoded every cubin/PTX in
`_dectc_codegen/` (cuobjdump/nvdisasm, no GPU); read the committed ledger/handoff docs entirely;
mined the jsonl transcripts (structure + sizes + targeted greps, NOT read-all). CPU-only throughout.

---

## 0. HEADLINE (what the upgrade IS, and where it lives)

The project ships an **UPGRADED L3-TC persistent-wgmma megakernel** whose tuned perf levers are
**BAKED as the `#ifndef` defaults in the kernel headers** (not passed at build time). The two
headline structural wins and the supporting dW win are all baked-on by default:

| Lever (macro) | Baked default | Win | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE` | **1** (entry-a deeper cp.async ring) | **+1.49×** (920.6→618.5 ms; roofline 4.35%→6.475%) | `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:186` |
| `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` | **4** (S=4 ring; >2 ⇒ dynamic smem) | (same KEEP) | `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:189` |
| `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE` | **1** (contiguous-layout staging) | **+2.05×** (1889.8→920.7 ms; roofline 2.08%→4.35%) | `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:145` |
| `SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S` | **8** (B1 sub-tiling) | **+4.02×** (5768→1434 ms; B1_barrier 51.2%→41.9%) | `model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:169` |
| `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK` | **1** (single-CTA dW; split-K obsoleted by DW_STAGE=1) | supersedes the older G=2 KEEP | `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:101` |

**Cumulative decoder: 1889→618 ms ≈ 3.05× from session start; roofline 2.08%→6.475%**
(`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:73-74`). These are NOT the scalar/naive path — the project uses ONLY the
pure-L3-TC persistent wgmma megakernel (`fused_{decoder,vit,mamba}_megakernel_tc<OptId>`), and the
above are the tuned upgrades to that path.

The **prebuilt `_ops.so` is the UPGRADED build** (statically confirmed — see §4): the shipped
decoder_tc cubin carries `SHARED:26384` + the `sg_dectc_pool` extern (the dynamic-smem deep-ring
path), not the 48 KB static baseline.

---

## 1. THE UPGRADED DECODER LEVERS — full mechanism + provenance

### 1.1 `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE` — the deeper cp.async ring (+1.49×)
`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:148-264` is the authoritative lever doc. A **3-way SELECTOR (0/1/2)**,
not a scale (`:227-252`):
- **PIPE=0** OFF — the shipped S=2 ring VERBATIM → byte-identical PTX (the `kRingAsync` cp.async
  double-buffer; the Track-A 0005 −14.2% win). At S=2 the deeper loop collapses to
  `cp_async_wait_group<0>` exactly, which is why OFF is byte-clean (`:173-175`).
- **PIPE=1** entry (a) — the SAME all-threads-stage / WG0-compute ring DEEPENED to
  `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` slots (keeps S−1 cp.async groups in flight). **The baked winner.**
- **PIPE=2** entry (b) — the producer/consumer mbarrier engine (transcribed from
  `tile_pipeline.cuh`; WG0 pure producer, WG1 pure consumer). **LOST the tournament: 857 vs 618 ms**
  (`:186`, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:78`, `SESSION_STATE.md:38`).

**Why it works (the mechanism that the campaign validated):** fwd/dX are **DRAIN/latency-bound**
(the OPPOSITE of the staging-bound dW that sank the reverted P0). Confirmed via a new `--fwd-fine`
sub-profiler BEFORE building (doctrine): pre-KEEP fwd ring WAIT 43% vs WGMMA 31%, dX WAIT 56% vs 20%
→ deeper prefetch hides the cp.async drain (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:64-67`). You can hide a WAIT
behind more in-flight loads; you cannot hide 97% staging behind 3% MMA (`:71-73`). **Parity by
construction:** the deeper ring reorders LOADS only; the wgmma ISSUE sequence (ascending-k, k=0
overwrite / k>0 accumulate) is unchanged → fp32 accumulation bit-identical (`:168-175`).

**Three ring bodies** live in `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`
(`CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md:138`): the producer/consumer mbarrier engine (`:860-987`), the original S=2
double-buffer (`:988-1016`), and the deeper RS=3..4 ring (`:1017-1062`, uses
`cp_async_wait_group<RS-2>` steady / `<0>` tail).

### 1.2 The static→dynamic smem conversion (the UNBLOCKER for STAGES≥3)
`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:426-492` (also `CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md:140`). The static
`__shared__ DecTcSmem` is hard-capped at **48 KB** on H100; the deeper ring's `sA`/`sB` grow ∝ ring
depth (`:386-387`), and the legal-max tile (TILE_M=256/N=128/IL=4) reaches **49.64 KB at S=4** —
the one config that busts the static cap. Preprocessor gate:
```
#if (SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE && (SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES > 2))
#define SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM 1   // fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:464-468
```
When ON, `DecTcSmem` is placed in an `extern __shared__ char[]` pool (the `sg_dectc_pool` symbol),
the func opts in via `cudaFuncSetAttribute(..., cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize,
sizeof(DecTcSmem))`, and occupancy≥1 is certified against the real size vs the **228 KB/SM** dynamic
budget. Allocation change only — identical layout / access / fp32 order / wgmma issue → parity by
construction (`:439-442`). A compile-time `static_assert(sizeof(DecTcSmem) <= 48*1024)` guards the
gate-OFF path (`:478-485`) so a future config that would silently hit "too many resources" surfaces
as an honest build error.
**Measured sizeof(DecTcSmem)** (nvcc sm_90a, recorded in the source `:461-463`):
default TILE 128/128/IL2 — S=2 17.64 / S=3 25.64 / **S=4 33.64 KB**; legal-max 256/128/IL4 —
S=2 25.64 / S=3 37.64 / **S=4 49.64 KB(*)** (* the only >48 KB case → exactly what the gate routes).

This conversion is what made the +1.49× possible: an earlier attempt (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:107-127`)
REJECTED PIPE=1/STAGES≥3 as "resource-blocked" ("too many resources requested for launch") and
root-caused it (2026-06-17) to the **static 48 KB cap** (NOT smem-competition, NOT registers — fails
at S=3 even with dW-staging OFF and cons_regs=168), then queued + landed the static→dynamic fix.

### 1.3 `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1` — contiguous-layout dW staging (+2.05×, the FIRST major win)
`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:117-146`. The dW GEMM (dW=dYᵀ·X, K=T) is **STAGING-bound, not
drain-bound**: ~97% of each K-step was the scalar transposed-strided operand gather, ~3% the wgmma.
DW_STAGE=1 does a cheap grid-cooperative **pre-transpose** (`dectc_dw_transpose_operands`) writing
each weight's dY/X ONCE per step into K-contiguous bf16 scratch (`dYt[Nout,K]`,`Xt[Kin,K]`,
16B-aligned), so the dW then reuses the proven cp.async ring's 16-byte coalesced copies instead of
the 2-byte strided gather. Transport-only → fp64 parity + A/A/A by construction. **KEY REFRAME
(`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:61`): the megakernel's ~2% roofline was a STAGING artifact, not a hardware
ceiling.** This SUPERSEDED the Track-C split-K=2 KEEP → DW_SPLITK default reset to **1** (single-CTA
dW now 2.05× faster than G=2-scalar; split-K was only a scalar-dW grid-fill mitigation).
`kDecDwTransposeActive = (DW_STAGE==1) && (DW_SPLITK==1)` (`CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md:149`).

### 1.4 The reverted P0 (the mechanism lesson behind all of the above)
`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:52`: the original **P0 decoder dW pipelined GEMM** (mbarrier
producer/consumer on dW) PASSED fp64 (11/11) but REGRESSED perf −11.6% (1921.8→2144.8 ms), and
depth-3/4 wouldn't launch. Root cause = dW is 97%-staging/3%-MMA → can't hide staging behind MMA,
and the producer/consumer split STOLE the staging threads. This redirected the whole campaign:
**the lever is faster STAGING (→ the +2.05× DW_STAGE), and pipelining only helps the drain-bound
fwd/dX (→ the +1.49× deeper ring)**. PIPE=2 (the producer/consumer engine ported to fwd/dX) was
kept as a tournament ENTRY and LOST to the simpler deeper-ring (857 vs 618).

---

## 2. THE UPGRADED ViT LEVER — `SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S=8` (+4.02×)

`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:125-170` (lever doc) + `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:588-613` (the P1 loop).
**The #1 ViT lever by far.** ViT's GEMM tile is locked at `kTileM = LCM(kSeq=17, 64) = 1088` rows
(a tile boundary must be both a wgmma-m64 boundary AND a whole-sample boundary). At B=1024 →
T=17408 → only **n_tiles=16** P1 tiles, so **116 of 132 CTAs do ZERO P1 work and spin at B1** the
whole fwd+bwd. This is **tile-count-vs-SM quantization** (NOT intra-tile skew): B1_barrier = 51.2%
of the step (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:149-158`, the profiled ViT bottleneck map). The lever decouples
P1 SCHEDULING granularity from the 1088 GEMM lock: P1 grid-strides over sub-tiles of **S whole
samples** (`kSeq·S` rows) instead of whole 1088-row tiles, growing n_tiles ~(64/S)×. S must stay a
whole-sample count (`static_assert :238-240` — never split a 17-row sample, that corrupts
attention). The sub-tile rows are generally not ÷64, so small GEMMs pad M to `ceil(rows/64)·64` with
a runtime `m_real` row-guard (race-free, inert pad rows).

**Default 64** (= kSamplesPerTile) ⇒ byte-identical OFF build (the m_real guard + runtime-m_atoms
code is `#if SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S < 64`'d out entirely). **Baked verdict 64→8** (2026-06-17,
`:164-169`): S=8 is parity-clean (11/11 ViT cells × 3 seeds {42,7,123}; A/A/A held — S is a fixed
deterministic partition) AND fastest — **4.02× vs S=64 OFF at d=2048/B=1024**; B1_barrier
51.2%→41.9%; U-shaped curve inflects at 8 (S=4 ticks back +1.2%). **Parity surface:** dW/biases/cls/
pos grads byte-identical (P2 reads acts by global token row, ascending-k); the 10 LN-affine γ/β grads
+ loss are valid fp32 REASSOCIATIONS absorbed by the gate's 1e-4 reorder tol (`:150-162`).

**Note — the ViT win-number is reported two ways in the docs (a reconcile point, not a contradiction):**
`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:151` and `SESSION_STATE.md:26` give **5768→1434 ms ≈ 4.02×** as the wall-step;
the same 4.02× is also described as the B1_barrier *share* dropping 51.2%→41.9% (`:167`). The 4.02×
is the wall-clock step speedup; the 51.2%→41.9% is the residual barrier share after the fix.

**The ViT dW-staging twin was a REVERT** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:80-105`): the verbatim port of the
decoder +2.05× dW win to ViT gave only +4.5% AND went gate-RED on supergrok2/vit — because ViT is
